category: Enterprise Architecture, System Hardening & Advanced Threats

content.tldr: The attack lifecycle follows reconnaissance, weaponization, exploitation, privilege escalation, persistence, and exfiltration, countered by defenders at each stage using the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
content.simple_explanation: Adversary operations follow a structured sequence: 1) Reconnaissance (scanning OSINT, IP ranges, exposed services); 2) Weaponization & Exploitation (delivering tailored exploits against identified vulnerabilities); 3) Privilege Escalation (exploiting local misconfigurations or kernel bugs to gain root/SYSTEM); 4) Persistence (installing cron jobs, services, or registry keys); 5) Lateral Movement (harvesting credentials via Mimikatz to access neighboring servers); and 6) Objective Execution (ransomware encryption or exfiltration). Defenders map detections directly to these MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
content.real_world_example: A bank robbery operation: casing the building for camera blind spots, picking the rear door lock, overriding alarm panels, opening internal vault gates, and loading cash into a getaway vehicle.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Defenders only need to break one single link in the attack chain to disrupt an entire intrusion. Detecting and responding early during reconnaissance or lateral movement prevents critical data exfiltration.
